title: Effects of acoustic environment on design work performance based on multitask visual cognitive performance in office space
authors: Qi Meng, Yuying An, Da Yang, 2021
research_question: What are the effects of different sound source types, sound pressure levels (SPLs), and reverberation times (RTs) on multitask visual cognitive performance in design offices, and how do individual characteristics (gender, noise sensitivity, personality traits, and musical preference) affect this performance?

participants.description: 41 college students majoring in architecture or interior design from Harbin Institute of Technology (18 women, mean age = 24.43 years, SD = 2.47; 23 men, mean age = 24.01 years, SD = 2.56). All participants passed hearing and vision tests.
participants.recruitment: Selected as respondents from a specific university department.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Five representative sound sources: speech, traffic noise, natural sound, air-conditioning noise, and music. 'Ambient environment' (background noise <7 dBA) served as a reference. SPLs were adjusted to 50 dBA for sound source type comparison. For SPL effects, traffic noise and air-conditioning noise were presented at 45, 50, 55, 60, 65 dBA. For RT effects, speech and music were presented at 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, 1.2, 1.5 s RT. Audio clips were 5 min long and played through a headset.

Multitask visual cognitive task developed using E-prime (Experimenters Prime 3.0) suite. Tasks included visual search (finding target among closed rings), graphical memory (identifying shape), and location memory (identifying quadrant). Each task included 135 graphics, with 30 tasks per respondent.

mechanisms: Human working efficiency is highest at a medium arousal level.
Natural sound can alleviate work pressure and cause inattention.
Noise can strengthen concentration ability and resistance to noise interference.
High noise levels lead to rapid increases in physiological and mental health losses.
Mental fatigue caused by low-frequency noise (air-conditioning noise) impacts psychophysiological and working memory responses.
Increased reverberation time (RT) leads to decreased speech clarity, which reduces speech interference on work performance.
Low speech intelligibility results in auditory distraction.
Increased RT allows for more attention to visual cognition work.
implementation_implications: Music sound can be used to mask other noises in office spaces.
Speech intelligibility should be reduced in office designs.
Natural sounds, such as flowing stream water, should be avoided in indoor soundscapes as they interfere with visual perception.
Traffic noise SPL should be controlled at 50 dBA.
Air-conditioning noise SPL should be controlled at 55 dBA.
Outer window glasses should be selected based on local traffic noise levels.
Architects should adjust the distance between air-conditioning noise sources and employees.
Reverberation time should be appropriately increased in office spaces to reduce speech interference.
Room acoustic design should be adjusted to improve visual cognitive work performance based on individual characteristics.
Office space designs should consider individual characteristics, work habits, and employee needs when arranging employees in suitable working environments.

limitations: The study's experimental design was limited in complexity and length, restricting the number of noise sources investigated (only traffic noise and air-conditioning noise for SPL effects).
Future work should extend to other sound sources (e.g., natural sound, music) for SPL effects and explore underlying mechanisms in more detail.
